issues.legal_issue: Proceeds from selling trees are capital rather than income when the trees are removed with their roots so that the source of further growth and recurring returns is destroyed.
material_facts: The dispute arose from an agricultural income-tax assessment that included proceeds from the sale of teak trees.
The trees had been planted years earlier and were cut and completely removed from the land together with their roots.
The trees were removed to plant rubber, and there was no possibility of their regeneration or of further recurring income from them.
issues.conclusion: The sale proceeds were capital in nature and not agricultural income; the appeals were allowed and the High Court’s judgment was set aside. The Court found it unnecessary to answer the separate question about deductions for expenses.
issues.legal_principle: Income ordinarily connotes a periodical monetary return received with some regularity, or expected regularity, from a definite source whose object is to produce a return. When trees are removed with their roots and the possibility of regeneration is eliminated, the source of further returns ceases and the disposal affects the capital structure, so the proceeds are capital rather than revenue. A profit motive does not by itself make a capital accretion taxable income. The Court applied the distinction in Commissioner of Income-tax, Bengal v. Messrs. Shaw Wallace and Company, distinguished V. Venugopala Verma Rajah v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Kerala, where stumps capable of regeneration remained, and relied on the capital-structure analysis in Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay South v. V. T. Patwardhan. The dispute arose under the Kerala Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1950, and came by reference under section 60(1); no substantive provision defining agricultural income was identified in the judgment.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_assessment_dispu: A taxpayer challenged the inclusion of sale proceeds in an agricultural income-tax assessment.
predicates.trees_removed_with_roots: The taxpayer sold trees that had been cut and removed from the land together with their roots.
predicates.no_regeneration_or_recurring_returns: Removing the trees and roots left no possibility of regeneration or further recurring returns from those trees.
predicates.sale_receipts_are_capital_not_revenue: The proceeds from selling the trees are treated as capital receipts rather than revenue income.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer disputes inclusion of tree-sale proceeds in an agricultural income-tax assessment and the trees were removed with their roots so that no regeneration or recurring returns remained possible, the proceeds are treated as capital rather than revenue.
